region.name: Board and Partner Communications
region.summary: Drafts and prep for board deck engineering slides, investor and data-room narratives, Pillar Bank remediation plans, incident all-hands, and outbox-pattern blog content covering hiring plans, SOC 2 status, ACH incidents, and Sidekiq migration.

brief.text:
This region collects drafts and prep materials for Stencil's outward-facing and leadership communications: the engineering section of the board deck, investor and data-room narratives (including a SOC 2 status letter from CTO Maya Chen to Northfield Ventures), the Pillar Bank remediation plan, the incident all-hands talk, and an engineering blog post on the outbox pattern. The board deck's engineering use-of-funds section commits to 12 engineering hires over 9 months across payments, mobile, and data. It also covers a VP Engineering search with finalists in references, moving all money-moving jobs off Sidekiq, and an explicit statement that no Postgres sharding project is planned. Slides 4-5 flag hiring risks: a 55% offer-accept rate, below-market senior iOS bands, and a payments bus factor. They also list SOC 2 Type II gaps and deadlines, the card soft launch deferred to Q1 2027, and Q4 priorities. Personal deck notes record that Series B is out of scope and that there is no architecture slide. They also flag the GA date vs. board meeting timing as a risk, along with open GA blockers. Pending items include Marcus's ACH metrics, a headcount check, a final read, and an open question on whether to disclose ACH volume scale numbers.

On SOC 2, the Type I report is dated June 30, 2026 and the Type II observation window runs July 1 to December 31, 2026. Communications must never claim a Type II report exists. The letter covers three readiness-review gaps (including access reviews and vendor risk assessments), the September 26 SEV1 duplicate debit incident, and program ownership. The highest-severity open items in this region concern access reviews: the Q3 access review is likely to become a Type II exception (risk severity 28), and Sam owns a todo to confirm it reaches 100% (severity 28). A separate open risk covers fractional share position mismatches (severity 18).

The Pillar Bank remediation plan has several open questions. One is whether to commit to a sweep migration date, currently leaning toward 2026-12-15 with a fallback. Others are whether to list all money-moving jobs in an appendix, who represents Stencil in the weekly ops sync, and whether the draft incident-notification language commits too strongly. The incident all-hands prep requires Marcus's review, asking Devon whether he is comfortable being named, and building a one-slide timeline. Q&A will have no cap, and whether to mention Pillar's remediation request is still undecided. The outbox blog draft is half-written. It describes the dual-write problem and the April 6 ACH batch stall that caused missed NACHA cutoffs and late deposits. The pattern it explains writes transfer and outbox rows in one Postgres transaction, uses a worker publishing to SQS FIFO, and relies on an idempotent consumer. The hard parts it covers are autovacuum contention that delayed cut-over by seven weeks, two weeks of shadow mode, and NACHA cutoff-relative lag alerting. Aleks must approve any mention of Pillar or specific numbers. Typical questions for this region include what the board was told about hiring or Sidekiq, what may be said about SOC 2 status, what the Pillar remediation plan commits to, and what remains blocked before publishing or presenting.

items.title: Open Question: Commit to a date for sweep migration?
